annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kovacic, M.; Marvin, S.; While, A.
key_provisions_or_claims: Californian municipalities have adopted prohibitive, permissive and collaborative approaches to regulating sidewalk delivery robots.
Palo Alto requires encroachment permits, operator liability, $2-4M insurance and 24-hour reporting of significant collisions.
Early-mover firms such as Starship strongly shaped permitting rules, including state legislation in 2019.
Campus precinct trials serve as semi-enclosed test beds with bespoke regulation.
Sidewalk robots require new regulatory frameworks distinct from e-scooters and AVs.
annotation.summary_en: Journal article analysing how Californian municipalities regulate sidewalk delivery robots, using policy analysis and interviews. It identifies prohibitive, permissive and collaborative regulatory approaches, including permit, liability and insurance requirements, and discusses the influence of first-mover firms on rules.
annotation.title_clean: Regulating sidewalk delivery robots as a disruptive new urban technology
annotation.title_en: Regulating sidewalk delivery robots as a disruptive new urban technology
